project.name: Online Library Management System
project.summary: Web platform for members to search, borrow, return, and renew books, with librarian administration and automated email reminders.

functional_requirements: System sends email reminders before due dates
non_functional_requirements: The system shall be easy to use with an intuitive UI
The system shall enforce authentication and role‑based access control
The system shall be reliable with 99.9% uptime
The system shall respond to user actions within 2 seconds

actors.name: Member
actors.description: A registered user who searches, borrows, returns, and renews books

actors.name: Librarian
actors.description: Staff who manages books, members, loans and collects fines

actors.name: Email Service
actors.description: External service that sends due‑date reminder emails

use_cases.name: Search Catalogue
use_cases.description: Member queries the catalogue by title, author or keyword and views results

use_cases.name: Borrow Book
use_cases.description: Member selects an available book and creates a loan record

use_cases.name: Return Book
use_cases.description: Member returns a borrowed book, triggering inventory update and fine calculation if overdue

use_cases.name: Manage Inventory
use_cases.description: Librarian adds, updates, or removes book records and manages member accounts

use_cases.name: Send Due Reminder
use_cases.description: Email Service dispatches reminder emails to members three days before loan due dates

criteria: Search results are returned within 2 seconds
Results can be filtered by title, author, or keyword
System verifies book availability before creating loan
Loan record includes member ID, book ID, and due date
Inventory count is incremented upon return
Overdue fines are calculated and displayed to the member
Renewal is allowed only if no other member has placed a hold
Due date is extended by the maximum allowed renewal period

acceptance_criteria.requirement: System sends email reminders before due dates
criteria: Reminder email is sent exactly 3 days prior to due date
Email contains due date, book title, and a link to the member portal

user_stories.story: As a member, I want to search the catalogue, so that I can find books of interest.
acceptance_criteria: Search returns results matching title, author, or ISBN.
Results are displayed within 2 seconds.

user_stories.story: As a member, I want to borrow books, so that I can read them at home.
acceptance_criteria: Member can borrow up to the allowed limit of books.
Borrowed books are recorded with a due date.

user_stories.story: As a member, I want to return books, so that I can fulfill my loan obligations.
acceptance_criteria: Returned books are marked as available in the catalogue.
Any overdue fines are calculated at return.

user_stories.story: As a member, I want to renew loans, so that I can extend my reading time without visiting the library.
acceptance_criteria: Renewal is allowed only if no other member has placed a hold.
New due date is updated and communicated to the member.

user_stories.story: As a librarian, I want to manage books, members, and loans and collect fines, so that the library operates efficiently.
acceptance_criteria: Librarian can add, edit, or remove book records and member accounts.
System tracks loans and automatically calculates and records overdue fines.

user_stories.story: As a system, I want to send email reminders before due dates, so that members are aware of upcoming returns.
acceptance_criteria: Reminder emails are sent 3 days before the due date.
Emails contain book title, due date, and renewal link.

Database Designer.sql:
CREATE TABLE Members (
    member_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    email TEXT,
    join_date DATETIME,
    is_active BOOLEAN
);

CREATE TABLE Books (
    book_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    title TEXT,
    author TEXT,
    isbn TEXT,
    copies_total INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE Loans (
    loan_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    member_id INTEGER,
    book_id INTEGER,
    loan_date DATETIME,
    due_date DATETIME,
    returned_date DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (member_id) REFERENCES Members(member_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (book_id) REFERENCES Books(book_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Librarians (
    librarian_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT,
    email TEXT,
    hire_date DATETIME
);

Project Structure.architecture: A modular monolith where the React/Vite SPA communicates with FastAPI via REST/JSON. FastAPI handles authentication, business logic, and interacts with PostgreSQL through SQLAlchemy. Alembic manages schema migrations. Redis caches catalog queries and stores session data. Docker composes services for reproducible deployment. Email reminders are scheduled background tasks using Celery or FastAPI's background workers.
Project Structure.architecture_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A[User Browser] -->|HTTP| B[React SPA]
    B -->|API Calls| C[FastAPI Backend]
    C -->|ORM| D[PostgreSQL]
    C -->|Cache| E[Redis]
    C -->|Email Service| F[SMTP Server]
    C -->|Background Worker| G[Task Scheduler]
    G -->|Reminders| F

Documentation.readme: Online Library Management System (OLMS) enables members to search, borrow, return, and renew books. Librarians manage catalog, members, loans, and fines. Email reminders are sent before due dates. The app prioritizes usability, security, and reliability.
Documentation.api_documentation: GET /books?query= - search catalog; GET /books/{id} - book details; POST /loans - borrow (memberId, bookId); PUT /loans/{id}/return - return; PATCH /loans/{id}/renew - extend due date; GET /members/{id}/loans - view member loans; POST /fines/pay - pay overdue fine; POST /notifications/reminder - trigger email reminder.
Documentation.installation: Clone repo, run `npm install` (Node.js 18+). Set up PostgreSQL DB, run `npm run migrate`. Configure .env with DB credentials, SMTP settings, JWT secret. Start with `npm start`.
Documentation.deployment: Containerize with Docker; use Dockerfile provided. Deploy to any cloud (AWS ECS, Azure App Service, GCP Cloud Run). Use PostgreSQL managed instance. Set environment variables for DB URL and email service. Enable HTTPS via reverse proxy.
Documentation.sprint_plan: Sprint 1: Core CRUD for books and members, authentication. Sprint 2: Loan workflow, due date logic, fine calculation. Sprint 3: Email reminder service, UI polishing. Sprint 4: Security hardening, testing, CI/CD pipeline.
Documentation.architecture: Three‑tier: Frontend (React), API layer (Express.js), Data layer (PostgreSQL). JWT for auth, role‑based access (member, librarian). Email service via Nodemailer. Services communicate via REST; Docker Compose orchestrates containers.
